goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: User-facing claim: a human can create and adjust Type, Select, Drag, and multi-target Hold cues on the unified canvas while agents use the same durable operations, with deterministic browser-native CSS and safe history. T013 closes the last gate: attached Hold eligibility is derived from stored source replacement data, valid boundary edits retain both targets and persist exact generated coverage, and invalid boundaries disable submission with visible feedback and no revision change before recovery. Independent Chrome, visual, focused, privacy, and protected-file checks pass, with no regression in Drag, keyboard, boundaries, metadata, claims, history, reduced motion, diagnostics, or determinism. Final PM QA may begin; slice completion still requires T005 and T999.
evidence: Attached-Hold eligibility — PASS: apps/editor/src/main.ts:1577-1604 derives valid edited boundaries from the attached cue’s stored replacement tracks, applications, bindings, slots, and keyframes rather than cue-generated document tracks.

Invalid-boundary atomicity and recovery — PASS: refreshHoldTargetOptions at apps/editor/src/main.ts:1606-1623 removes unavailable targets, disables submission through the normal render path, emits explicit error feedback naming the boundary and unchanged revision, and restores attached semantic targets when a valid boundary returns.

Installed Chrome proves the exact regression path at apps/editor/tests/phase4-reusable-cues.spec.ts:80-110: create a two-target Hold at 1000 ms; edit to invalid 900 ms; observe disabled submission, error status, and revision 1; restore valid 0 ms; retain both targets; commit revision 2; reload; and verify enterMs plus semantic/generated target equality.

Exact Hold coverage remains PASS: every selected target must contribute source tracks; mixed unanimated and missing-boundary scopes reject with exact reason codes and unchanged service revision; two independent animated targets produce generated tracks covering both stable IDs.

Intermediate Drag remains PASS: the editor creates three waypoints, directly drags the middle waypoint, preserves the CLI-authored intermediate through reload and form edits, and proves exact undo/redo.

Keyboard and responsive evidence remains PASS: installed Chrome uses real Home/ArrowDown events on the focused fallback select and checks unified workspace visibility and horizontal containment at 760 px and 1280 px widths.

Boundary proof remains PASS: installed Chrome visual proof records 29 t-1/t/t+1 samples, 30 expected semantic assertions across Type, Select, Drag, and Hold, two identical raster runs, 19 distinct rasters, and zero repeated pixel drift.

Native-preview and reduced-motion evidence remains PASS: iframe srcdoc equals compiled HTML, positive browser-created CSSAnimation inventory is asserted before reduction, and the final reduced-motion inventory is zero.

Durable parity/history remains PASS: reload, claimed agent update, stale and unauthorized rejection, per-family detach/delete/undo/redo, and exact compiled-byte preservation are exercised through the service-backed editor/CLI path.

Independent verification passed: installed-Chrome browser workflow 1/1; visual proof 1/1; focused domain/protocol/CLI suites 31/31. The current sanitized browser receipt reports revision 35, four cues, and zero runtime, failed-request, HTTP, or unexpected-network diagnostics.

T013 recorded byte-identical installed-Chrome receipts across two runs with SHA-256 dc4ef6e8a990f1fa40913d1c4d4ee4b2d2bf3fbf8ab18d127337c8649738d14f; receipt structure remains timestamp- and path-free.

Sensitive-content and containment checks pass: findingCount=0 across tracked/diff/index/worktree/untracked; private-ignore targetCount=3, ignoredCount=3, trackedPrivateCount=0; protected-file diff and git diff --check pass; no Slice 3 or Phase 5 implementation appears.
Failure mode 1, cue metadata/track drift or editor/CLI divergence — PASS: exact Hold and Drag target/waypoint coverage, durable reload, atomic rejection, detach, and history are directly asserted.

Failure mode 2, hidden canvas gaps or incorrect native boundaries — PASS: canvas target/path editing, attached Hold adjustment, genuine keyboard fallback, responsive containment, native preview, and every expected boundary are exercised.

Failure mode 3, private leakage or green tests masking browser/reduced-motion failures — PASS at this gate: sanitized deterministic receipts, comprehensive browser diagnostics, reduced-motion inventory, privacy scans, and protected-file checks are clean.
